payload.title: What Are the Serbian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Serbian wedding traditions in the order the day unfolds, from the prosidba and the kum to the Orthodox crowning and the kolo, with notes for Australians marrying in Serbia or at home.
key_takeaways: The church service is set by the Serbian Orthodox Church, while the folk customs around it vary by family and region.
The kum is the first of two church witnesses and exchanges the rings, a far larger role than the English "best man" suggests.
The service centres on rings, crowns, a white cloth binding the couple's right hands, a shared cup of wine and a threefold walk around the table.

Smartraveller rates Serbia "Exercise normal safety precautions" as at November 2026, and paperwork for a legal wedding there should be checked with the registry and the Australian Embassy in Belgrade.

faq.a: A sequence of family customs around a Serbian Orthodox church service: the prosidba, collecting the bride, the wedding, and her arrival at her new home. The church rite is set by the Church; the folk customs vary by family and region.

faq.q: What does the kum do at a Serbian wedding?
faq.a: The kum is the first of two church witnesses, with the stari svat. He attests at the pre-marriage examination that there is no impediment, exchanges the rings during the betrothal and, with the stari svat, holds the couple's candles until the service ends.

faq.q: Why do Serbian couples wear crowns at the wedding?
faq.a: The crowning gives the service its name, venčanje, from venac, a wreath. Wreaths were once used; today it is mostly crowns. For what the crowns mean in your parish, ask your priest.

faq.q: What happens with the apple at a Serbian wedding?
faq.a: As it is often told, an apple is set high and the groom or his party tries to hit it before the bride is led out. It is a folk custom that varies by family, not part of the church service.
A collective circle dance, inscribed by UNESCO for Serbia in 2017, in which dancers link hands in a chain and move to music. Guests learn it by joining in.

Smartraveller rates Serbia "Exercise normal safety precautions" as at November 2026. For a legal wedding, ask the Serbian authorities what proof of no impediment they accept and check with the registry and the Australian Embassy in Belgrade, including any fees.

faq.q: What should guests wear to a Serbian wedding?
faq.a: There is no single dress code, so follow the invitation. For the church, ask the couple what their parish expects, and wear shoes you can dance the kolo in.
